title: Fix voucher redemption race condition using pessimistic locking
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
# Fix: Voucher Redemption Race Condition

Fix voucher redemption race condition using pessimistic locking

Problem:
- Voucher validation occurred before acquiring database lock
- Multiple concurrent requests could all see voucher as 'available'
- Led to over-redemption beyond max_usages limit

Solution:
- Added select_for_update() to acquire row-level lock before validation
- Added explicit availability check after lock acquisition
- Ensures only one thread can validate voucher state at a time

Fixes #1398


- Tested: 5 concurrent threads redeemed voucher with max_usages=3

## Summary by Sourcery

Prevent race conditions during voucher redemption by validating availability under a database row lock.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure voucher availability is checked under a row-level lock to prevent over-redemption under concurrent requests.

Enhancements:
- Use pessimistic locking on voucher rows when computing availability in the cart service.

title: Feat: Import schedule and speakers
author: ArnavBallinCode
body: # End-to-End Speaker/Session CSV Import + Organizer Schedule Editor Fixes This PR adds a complete organizer-side import flow for **speakers** and **sessions** from CSV, including mapping UI, async processing, data upsert logic, and schedule assignment support. It also fixes organizer-only rendering issues in the schedule editor that could make sessions appear in public/frontend schedule views but not in the organizer editor. ## What was happening before - Organizers had no full CSV import workflow for speakers/sessions in the navigation and orga views. - Session import did not reliably create or recover rooms for scheduling. - Async “processing” waiting pages could get stuck on transient backend errors. - Organizer schedule editor could show an empty grid when talk dates were outside event start/end window, even though sessions existed and rendered in other schedule views. - Some schedule API room description payloads could be null-like and break strict editor parsing. ## What this PR changes ### 1) Organizer CSV import flows (new end-to-end UX) - Adds organizer navigation entries for speaker/session import. - Adds routes and views for: - Speaker CSV upload and column mapping flow. - Session CSV upload and column mapping flow. - Adds import templates for upload + mapping + preview/process pages. ### 2) New import mapping forms - Adds reusable CSV import form utilities and concrete mapping forms for speakers and sessions. - Supports CSV header normalization, suggestions, and static values. - Persists import mapping settings via event settings so organizers do not remap every run. - Supports mapping of dynamic submission questions (`question_` fields). ### 3) Async import task plumbing - Registers `talkimport` task module. - Adds robust async processing flow for speaker/session imports. - Returns structured import result summary (`created`, `updated`, `skipped`, `errors`) for user feedback. ### 4) Speaker import behavior - Upserts speakers by identifier/code and email fallback. - Applies optional profile/user fields (locale, avatar metadata, biography). - Creates/updates `SpeakerProfile` as needed. - Links imported speakers to submissions by code/pk/title references. ### 5) Session import behavior - Upserts sessions by code and title fallback. - Resolves submission type, track, state, tags, duration, locale, notes, and question answers. - Ensures talk slots exist for WIP schedule visibility. - Imports start/end when present. - Links speakers from mapped fields. - Resolves room by exact/fuzzy/pk match, undeletes soft-deleted rooms, and creates missing rooms. - Creates imported rooms with safe defaults and appends to in-memory caches for same-run reuse. ### 6) Organizer schedule editor rendering fixes - Fixes room description serialization for schedule API so empty descriptions are emitted safely. - Expands schedule editor day tabs to include **actual talk start dates**, not only event date bounds. - This fixes cases where sessions exist (and render in other schedule views) but do not appear in organizer editor due to date-window mismatch. ### 7) Async waiting-page resilience - Replaces fragile jQuery polling logic with fetch-based polling. - Adds retry/backoff and error recovery behavior. - Keeps redirect behavior once async task completes. - Removes now-unneeded jQuery include from waiting page template. ### 8) Config and platform updates - Increases CSV upload limit from 1 MB to 10 MB for import use cases. - Adds event URL helpers for new import endpoints. - Wires default settings for speaker/submission import mappings. ## What happens when (runtime flow) ### Speaker import 1. Organizer opens Speaker Import from orga nav. 2. Uploads CSV. 3. Maps columns in process form (with suggestions/static values). 4. Async task runs and upserts users/profiles and links to submissions. 5. Organizer gets completion message with created/updated/skipped/errors. ### Session import 1. Organizer opens Session Import from orga nav. 2. Uploads CSV. 3. Maps columns in process form. 4. Async task upserts submissions, ensures talk slots, links speakers, applies schedule fields. 5. Missing rooms are resolved/undeleted/created as needed. 6. Imported sessions become available in schedule editor and can be released. ### Schedule editor - Editor now computes visible day range from both: - event start/end, and - talk start dates in payload. - This prevents organizer-only “empty grid” when talk dates differ from event date window. ## Edge cases covered - Missing/expired uploaded CSV file. - Invalid or empty parsed CSV. - Missing required speaker/session identity fields. - Identifier/code overflow constraints. - Soft-deleted room recovery. - Duplicate room names in same import run. - Unknown state/type/track fallback behavior. - Transient async polling failures and temporary backend pressure. - Empty/null-like room descriptions in schedule payload. ## Summary Adds organizer CSV import for speakers and sessions with async processing and event-scoped mapping settings. ## Key Behavior - Imports run through Celery tasks and return created/updated/skipped/error summaries. - Missing/expired cached upload files now redirect safely back to upload step. - Speaker matching supports event profile by code, global user by code, and email fallback. - Session upsert is by code then title fallback. - Speaker-session linking works in both import orders (sessions->speakers and speakers->sessions). - Start/end/room mapping is applied to WIP talk slots when slot exists. ## Stability Fixes - Registered talk import tasks in Celery autodiscovery (`base/tasks.py`). - Sanitized row-level DB errors for user-facing responses. - Added length-safe handling/fallback for imported speaker/session IDs. ## Config - CSV upload size limit is validated via `MAX_SIZE_CONFIG[UPLOAD_SIZE_CSV]` (default currently 10 MB). ## Files Updated in Final Patch - app/eventyay/base/services/talkimport.py - app/eventyay/base/tasks.py - app/eventyay/orga/views/speaker.py - app/eventyay/orga/views/submission.py

title: Add .agents/skills AI agent system
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
Also partial part of #2737

!! Needs clarification of Deployment and Docker instructions. 

## Future Plan

We plan to further align with the Agent Skills specification and improve the quality, modularity, and execution capability of our skills.

### 1. Standardize Skill Structure

Move towards a richer, extensible structure:
```

skill-name/
├── SKILL.md          # Metadata + core instructions (kept concise)
├── scripts/          # Reusable executable helpers (e.g., validation, generation)
├── references/       # Detailed docs loaded only when needed
├── assets/           # Templates (API responses, serializers, etc.)
└── tests/ (optional) # Test cases for validating skill behavior

```
---

### 2. Improve Skill Quality

- Make all skills **atomic and composable**
- Ensure each skill has:
  - clear "When to use"
  - step-by-step execution
  - validation steps
  - project-specific gotchas
- Remove generic or redundant instructions
- Optimize for **agent execution, not human readability**

---

### 3. Introduce Progressive Disclosure

- Keep `SKILL.md` minimal (core logic only)
- Move heavy or conditional details into `references/`
- Explicitly guide when to load additional context

---

### 4. Add Execution Support via Scripts

- Extract repeated logic into `scripts/`
- Examples:
  - migration validation scripts
  - API scaffold generators
  - lint/test runners

This avoids the agent re-deriving logic each time.

---

### 5. Expand Context Layer

Extend `.agents/context/` beyond `architecture.md`:

- api-patterns.md
- data-modeling.md
- repo-conventions.md

This improves retrieval and reduces hallucination.

---

### 6. Introduce Skill Composition

- Enable chaining of skills for larger tasks
- Add higher-level "meta skills" (e.g., feature implementation)
- Ensure naming consistency for better triggering

---

### 7. Continuous Refinement Loop

- Iterate skills based on real usage
- Capture:
  - common failures
  - corrections
  - edge cases
- Feed these back into:
  - "Gotchas"
  - validation steps
  - scripts

---

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce an AI agent skills and context system and expand contributor guidance for JavaScript/Vue, Docker, and git workflows.

New Features:
- Add a structured AI agent skills index under `.agents/skills/` and a context index under `.agents/context/` for repository navigation, Django workflows, Docker deployment, and documentation updates.
- Define dedicated instruction files for Docker/Docker Compose usage and container-based development and production workflows.

Enhancements:
- Clarify AI agent policy precedence, designating `agents.md` as the single source of truth and documenting the new skills and context directories.
- Extend JavaScript instructions to cover TypeScript and Vue 3 apps and document frontend code locations and Vue conventions.
- Document branching, commit, and PR expectations in git commit instructions.

title: Use Django-allauth native social login flow
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
## Problem

Users created with username/password could not log in via WikiMedia OAuth even when their WikiMedia account used the same email address. They were redirected to `/accounts/3rdparty/signup/` instead of being logged in.

Two root causes:

**1. `OAuthReturnView` bypassed allauth entirely**
The old view called `User.objects.get_or_create(email=...)` directly, creating bare User objects with no `SocialAccount` or `EmailAddress` records. This meant allauth's email-based auto-connect had nothing to match against on subsequent logins.

**2. `MediaWikiProvider` discards email when `confirmed_email=False`**
The upstream provider's `extract_email_addresses()` returns `[]` when the Wikimedia account has `confirmed_email=False`. With no email addresses on the `SocialLogin`, allauth's `_lookup_by_email` never runs, the user is treated as new, and the signup form is shown.

**3. Email may be `null` regardless of `confirmed_email`**
When the OAuth consumer registered on meta.wikimedia.org lacks "View email address" permission, the profile API returns `email=null` even for confirmed accounts. This blocks email-based lookup entirely.

---

## Fix

### Remove `OAuthReturnView`
Deleted the custom view and its URL. `OAuthLoginView` now simply redirects to allauth's standard `mediawiki_login` URL, letting allauth own the full callback flow.

### `EventyayMediaWikiProvider`
Subclass of `MediaWikiProvider` with two overrides:
- `extract_email_addresses`: when `VERIFIED_EMAIL=True` in settings, returns the email as verified even if `confirmed_email=False`.
- `extract_extra_data`: always stores the raw email in `extra_data` (upstream sets it to `null` when unconfirmed).
- `package = "allauth.socialaccount.providers.mediawiki"` — required so allauth loads the upstream URL conf instead of deriving it from `__module__`, which would cause a `NoReverseMatch`.

### Username fallback in `pre_social_login`
When `email=null` (no email permission on the OAuth consumer), the standard email lookup returns nothing. `CustomSocialAccountAdapter.pre_social_login` now tries `User.objects.get(wikimedia_username=extra_data['username'])` as a fallback. If found, `sociallogin.user` is set directly. `_did_authenticate_by_email` is intentionally left `None` to prevent allauth from calling `wipe_password()` (which would break the user's existing username/password login).

### allauth settings
```python
SOCIALACCOUNT_EMAIL_AUTHENTICATION = True
SOCIALACCOUNT_EMAIL_AUTHENTICATION_AUTO_CONNECT = True
```
These enable allauth's built-in email-based user matching.

> **Note on SCOPE:** WikiMedia's OAuth2 implementation does not accept `openid` or `profile` as valid scope values — passing them returns `invalid_scope`. The default scope (no explicit `SCOPE` key) is sufficient to receive the full profile. Whether `email` is included in the response depends solely on whether the OAuth consumer was registered with "View email address" permission on meta.wikimedia.org — not on the requested scope. The username fallback covers the case where it is not.


### `backfill_emailaddress` management command
Pre-allauth users have no `EmailAddress` row. Without it, `_lookup_by_email` cannot verify the match. This one-time command creates verified primary `EmailAddress` rows for all affected users:
```
python manage.py backfill_emailaddress [--dry-run]
```

---

## OAuth callback flow

```
Click "Login with WikiMedia"
  → OAuthLoginView → /accounts/mediawiki/login/ → meta.wikimedia.org
  → User approves → /accounts/mediawiki/login/callback/
  → complete_login()
      → sociallogin_from_response()
          → EventyayMediaWikiProvider.extract_email_addresses()
              → email present + VERIFIED_EMAIL=True → [EmailAddress(verified=True)]
      → sociallogin.lookup()
          → _lookup_by_socialaccount()  (fast path, returning users)
          → _lookup_by_email()          (matches existing user by verified email)
      → pre_social_login()
          → require_provider_enabled()
          → lookup_by_wikimedia_username()  (fallback when email=null)
      → _authenticate()
          → is_existing=True  → _login() → user logged in ✓
          → is_existing=False → process_signup() (genuinely new user)
```

---

## How to test

**Reproduce the bug (on `dev`):**
1. Check out `dev`
2. Create a user with username/password using email address `X`
3. Configure WikiMedia OAuth in admin settings
4. Log out, click "Login with WikiMedia" using a WikiMedia account that has email `X`
5. → Redirected to signup form (**bug**)

**Verify the fix (on this branch):**
1. Check out `fix/use-allauth-native-social-login`
2. Run: `python manage.py backfill_emailaddress`
3. Set the WikiMedia username on the existing user:
   ```python
   User.objects.filter(email='X').update(wikimedia_username='<wikimedia-username>')
   ```
4. Log out, click "Login with WikiMedia"
5. → Logged in as the existing user, redirected to `/common/` ✓

The username fallback (step 3) is only needed if the OAuth consumer lacks email permission. If it has email permission, step 3 can be skipped and the fix works via email matching alone.

---


## Problem

Users who registered with username/password could not log in via WikiMedia OAuth even when their WikiMedia account shared the same email address. They were redirected to the `/accounts/3rdparty/signup/` form instead of being logged in.

Two root causes:

**1. `email=null` in the WikiMedia API response**

The `/oauth2/resource/profile` endpoint only returns the `email` field when the OAuth consumer was registered with "View email address" permission AND the `email` scope is requested. Without this, the response has `confirmed_email: true` but `email: null`.

Because allauth's `_lookup_by_email()` only runs when `sociallogin.email_addresses` is non-empty, an empty list means the user is treated as new and routed to the signup form.

**2. `confirmed_email=False` support**

The upstream `MediaWikiProvider.extract_email_addresses()` discards the email entirely when `confirmed_email=False`. Many Wikimedia accounts have unconfirmed emails (pending re-confirmation after email change, etc.).

---

## Solution

### Layer 1 — Request the `email` scope

Added `SCOPE: ['openid', 'profile', 'email']` to `SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS['mediawiki']`. When the OAuth consumer has email permission, this causes Wikimedia to include the email in the profile response, enabling allauth's standard email-based user lookup.

> **Operator requirement**: the OAuth consumer registered on meta.wikimedia.org must have "View user's email address" permission enabled. Users may need to re-authorise after scope change.

### Layer 2 — `EventyayMediaWikiProvider` (trusts email when `VERIFIED_EMAIL=True`)

When `VERIFIED_EMAIL=True` is set (our default), `extract_email_addresses()` returns the email as verified even if `confirmed_email=False`. This allows allauth's `_lookup_by_email` to match an existing eventyay user by email.

`package = "allauth.socialaccount.providers.mediawiki"` is set explicitly so allauth loads the upstream `mediawiki.urls` URLconf instead of deriving it from `__module__` (which would produce a `NoReverseMatch`).

### Layer 3 — Username fallback in `pre_social_login`

When both layer 1 and 2 fail (email still null after scope fix, e.g. consumer has no email permission), `CustomSocialAccountAdapter.pre_social_login` queries `User.wikimedia_username` against `extra_data['username']` from the profile response.

If a match is found, `sociallogin.user` is set directly. `_did_authenticate_by_email` is intentionally left as `None` to prevent allauth's `_accept_login` from calling `wipe_password()`, which would break the user's existing username/password login.

### Layer 4 — `backfill_emailaddress` management command

Pre-allauth users have no `EmailAddress` row in `account_emailaddress`. Without it, `_lookup_by_email` cannot verify the match even when the email is returned. The management command creates verified primary `EmailAddress` rows for all such users:

```
python manage.py backfill_emailaddress [--dry-run]
```

---

## Lookup flow (OAuth callback)

```
WikiMedia callback → complete_login()
  → sociallogin.lookup()
      → _lookup_by_socialaccount()   # fast path for returning users
      → _lookup_by_email()           # requires email in response + EmailAddress row
  → CustomSocialAccountAdapter.pre_social_login()
      → require_provider_enabled()
      → lookup_by_wikimedia_username()  # fallback when email=null
  → _authenticate()
      → is_existing=True  → _login() → perform_login() → user logged in
      → is_existing=False → process_signup() (new account)
```

title: perf: replace schedule-JSON speakers page with server-rendered paginated view
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
Fixes #4776

## Description

This PR resolves the critical performance bottlenecks on the public speaker overview pages for large events. By replacing the heavy full-schedule JSON injection with a lightweight, paginated JSON API, we preserve the original UI while drastically improving load times and reducing payload sizes.

## What was optimized?

The previous implementation forced the backend to serialize the *entire* event schedule (all talks, rooms, tracks, and full speaker profiles) into a massive `schedule_json` blob injected into the HTML. This PR optimizes several key areas:

1. **HTML and embedded JSON payloads**: The massive `<script id="pretalx-schedule-data">` blob is completely removed from the DOM on the speakers page. The page HTML is now tiny and loads instantly.
2. **Server-side serialization work**: The backend no longer has to recursively query and serialize the entire schedule graph just to show a list of speakers. We now use a targeted `build_speaker_cards()` utility that queries only the necessary fields for a single page of speakers.
3. **Image transfers**: Instead of the browser eagerly trying to load all speaker avatars at once (or failing to lazy-load them efficiently from a massive DOM), the avatars are now fetched incrementally as the user scrolls.
4. **JavaScript parsing and rendering work**: The frontend Vue component (`SpeakersList.vue`) no longer freezes the main thread parsing a multi-megabyte JSON object. It now parses tiny, paginated API responses.
5. **Browser memory usage**: The browser only holds a fraction of the event data in memory at any given time, gracefully expanding the list via infinite scroll using `IntersectionObserver`.

## Implementation Details
- **Backend**: Added a `?format=json` response handler to the `SpeakerList` Django view, utilizing the existing `Filterable` ListView for native database-level pagination (48 speakers per page).
- **Frontend**: Preserved the original `<pretalx-schedule view="speakers">` component and its styling, but updated the inner `SpeakersList.vue` to fetch data asynchronously via the new API endpoint.
- **Cleanup**: Reverted previous experimental commits that attempted to switch to a pure Django server-rendered UI. This ensures the Vue layout, search, and filtering behaviors remain 100% intact.



https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0032d42-96d7-4c62-b740-71148a5549d0

## Summary by Sourcery

Replace full schedule injection on the public speakers page with a lightweight, server-paginated data flow while retaining the existing UI and interactions.

New Features:
- Add a paginated JSON endpoint for public speaker data, including profile, session, filtering, and pagination metadata.
- Support asynchronous speaker loading with infinite scroll while preserving the existing Vue speakers interface and filtering behavior.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent private speaker information, unpublished sessions, and data from other events from appearing in public speaker results.

Enhancements:
- Reduce speakers-page HTML payload, server-side serialization, browser parsing, and memory usage by replacing full schedule data with targeted speaker metadata and cards.
- Improve speaker search, sorting, language and track filtering, avatar loading, and session display for API-backed results.

Tests:
- Add coverage for paginated speaker responses, public-field handling, search and filter behavior, localization, pagination links, and HTML payload contents.

title: feat: auto-detection and cross-repo triggering for plugin dependency updates
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
fixes #5070 

## Background
Currently, the Eventyay deployment architecture uses a dual-mode system (BUILD_MODE=dev with --upgrade-package vs BUILD_MODE=production with --locked). While this works perfectly at build time, there is no active "detector" connecting the plugin repositories to the main eventyay repository.

When a PR is merged in a plugin repository, the Eventyay dev server does not automatically update because no new Docker build is triggered. This PR introduces the "Receiver" side of a Push model utilizing GitHub Actions `repository_dispatch`.

## Changes
- **Plugin Dispatch Receiver**: Creates a new workflow triggered by `on: repository_dispatch`. Depending on the target environment, it fulfills the security requirements:
  - **Dev Environment**: Triggers a new Docker build on the eventyay `dev` branch (which dynamically fetches the newest plugin commit).
  - **Main Environment**: Does not trigger a direct deployment. Instead, it triggers the `update-plugin-pins.yml` workflow to open a Pull Request updating `uv.lock`.

- **Lockfile Constraint Test**: Adds a CI test validating that `BUILD_MODE=production` (`uv sync --locked`) correctly rejects/ignores upstream git changes that aren't in the lockfile, proving that `--locked` successfully prevents auto-picking on main.

## Summary by Sourcery

Automate plugin update propagation across development and production workflows while verifying that production builds remain locked to reviewed dependency revisions.

New Features:
- Automatically respond to plugin repository updates by triggering development builds or lockfile update workflows based on the source branch.

Enhancements:
- Add CI verification that production Docker builds install plugin revisions matching the pinned lockfile commit.

CI:
- Add lockfile constraint tests for pushes and pull requests targeting the main and dev branches.

## Summary by Sourcery

Automate plugin update propagation across development and production workflows while keeping production dependency revisions locked and verifiable.

New Features:
- Automatically trigger development builds when plugin repositories dispatch update events from their dev branches.
- Automatically initiate reviewed lockfile update workflows for plugin releases from main or master branches.

Enhancements:
- Verify that production Docker builds install plugin revisions pinned in uv.lock.

CI:
- Add lockfile constraint checks for pushes and pull requests targeting the main and dev branches.

title: feat: smart LANCZOS-based image optimizations
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
This PR introduces a comprehensive image optimization pipeline for user uploads. It ensures that large image uploads are downscaled and re-encoded to optimal formats (WebP, PNG, or JPEG) to reduce bandwidth and storage usage while maintaining visual quality.

### Changes
*   **Centralized Encoder**: Added `encode_optimized` in `common/image.py` to standardize processing.
*   **Inline Optimization**: `UploadedFileField` now natively optimizes images for standard models (`picture`, `logo_image`, etc.).
*   **Settings Optimization**: `SettingsForm` now applies this optimization automatically to event and organizer configuration images.
*   **Backfill Command**: Refactored `backfill_images` to act as the single source of truth for retroactively optimizing all historical images, supporting dry-runs, precise model targeting (`--model`), and robust `MEDIA_ROOT`-safe backups (`--backup-dir`).
*   **Atomic Storage Updates**: Improved the local and remote file replacement logic in `process_image` to be safe and atomic.

### Testing
*   Added `max_size` enforcement to `RoomSerializer.picture`.
*   Tested end-to-end local generation, storage integration, and backfill edge-cases.
*   All Copilot code review comments resolved.

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement a centralized, safe image optimization pipeline for new uploads and historical media while adding room image support and interpretation-service synchronization.

New Features:
- Optimize uploaded event, organizer, room, product, and related images automatically using dimension-aware encoding and format selection.
- Add room picture uploads with validation and configured size limits.
- Add a room-admin action for synchronizing interpretation services.
- Extend the image backfill command to cover additional models and settings-backed images with model selection and dry-run support.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent unsafe image processing by rejecting corrupted, oversized, or decompression-bomb uploads.
- Make image replacement safer across local and remote storage backends and avoid unnecessary output growth.

Enhancements:
- Centralize image resizing, metadata removal, and optimized encoding in the common image-processing pipeline.
- Require backups outside MEDIA_ROOT for non-dry-run image backfills and update image-size guidance to the new limits.

Tests:
- Update room API expectations to include the picture field.

title: feat: Phase 1 (Core Cleanup) - Abolish commercial settings, fallback fees, and business UI from core
author: ArnavBallinCode
body: ## Linked PRs and integration checkout Phase 1 core cleanup. Pair this branch with [Business #95](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-business/pull/95) to test the Business Settings move. Core #6049 builds on this branch. For a combined test checkout, select these branches in the three independent repositories: | Repository | Branch | Includes | | --- | --- | --- | | fossasia/eventyay | test/phase2-ticketing-settings (#6049) | Core Phase 1 #5985 | | fossasia/eventyay-business (plugins/eventyay-business) | test/phase3-exclude-collected-fees (#97) | Business Phase 1B #95 | | fossasia/eventyay-stripe (plugins/eventyay-stripe) | test/phase2-smart-split (#49) | Stripe Phase 2B | The plugin directories have their own Git checkouts: switch each repository to the listed branch before testing the combined flow. For Phase 1 Business Settings alone, use core #5985 with Business #95. The Business Settings page is provided by the plugin at /admin/global/business/. **Release gate:** These drafts are integration work, not a complete billing cutover. The zero-rate legacy core monthly collector must be replaced by the Business-owned consolidated invoice in [Business Phase 3 #94](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-business/issues/94) before enabling live platform-fee collection. In particular, do not deploy Stripe #49 independently of the billing cutover. The upstream PRs target dev; the dependent source branches currently include their earlier phase commits and will be trimmed after parent PRs merge. Resolves #5984 Resolves Phase 1 of Epic #5890. This PR strictly decouples **all** commercial fee settings, fallback calculations, and Business UI configurations from the open-source core system. ### What was removed: 1. **Global Fee Fallbacks:** Ripped out `ticket_fee_percentage` and `ticket_fee_maximum` from `GlobalSettingsForm`. The background task calculator (`calculate_ticket_fee`) was purged of all logic and now explicitly calculates a $0 fee for all tickets. 2. **Stripe App Fees:** Ripped the Stripe Connect "App Fee" settings out of the `GlobalTicketingSettingsForm`. 3. **Global Business Settings View:** Completely removed the `GlobalBusinessSettingsForm` and its entire view. This takes the Stripe Organizer Billing Keys (Live & Test) out of the open-source core. ### Why: The open-source core platform must be 100% blind to FOSSASIA commercial SaaS logic. - The smart fee calculator and the Business Settings UI (including the Stripe Organizer Billing Keys) are moving to the `eventyay-business` plugin. - The platform fee is inherently **0%** if the business plugin is not installed. ## Summary by Sourcery Remove commercial fee management and business billing configuration from the core platform, leaving those capabilities to the business plugin. Enhancements: - Decouple commercial fee calculation, Stripe application fee configuration, and organizer billing settings from the open-source core. - Make core ticket fee calculation default to zero when the business plugin is unavailable. - Remove the core Business Settings page and redirect business navigation and voucher flows to the remaining business functionality. Tests: - Update control-panel tests to reflect the removal of commercial fee fields, settings, routes, and fee calculation coverage. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Settings** * The Business Settings page and its organizer billing credentials, billing validation, grace-period, and ticket-fee options are no longer available. * Stripe Connect application-fee percentage, minimum, and maximum settings have been removed from ticketing settings. * **Billing** * Monthly organizer invoices no longer include percentage-based ticket fees. Country-specific fee overrides and the global maximum fee no longer apply. * **Security** * Global Stripe billing secrets can no longer be revealed using organizer-level access. * **Navigation** * Business Settings has been removed from the Business menu. Legacy business settings links redirect to vouchers, and voucher changes return to the admin voucher list. **Related PR:** [fossasia/eventyay-business#95](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-business/pull/95) (Phase 1B)

title: Add neutral platform fee policy signal
author: ArnavBallinCode
body:
## Summary

- add a neutral Core signal for resolving an optional platform fee policy
- return an explicit zero-fee policy when no plugin responds
- validate fee percentages and caps
- reject invalid responses and multiple fee providers instead of applying an ambiguous fee

## Context

This is the Core foundation for the plugin decoupling tracked in [#5890](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay/issues/5890).

Core does not check for or import `eventyay-business`. It only defines the signal, response type, and resolver. The companion PRs are:

1. [eventyay-business#99](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-business/pull/99), which registers the Business fee-policy provider;
2. [eventyay-stripe#55](https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-stripe/pull/55), which consumes this resolver and removes direct Business app, model, and service imports.

This PR does not change payment behavior by itself.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/base/test_platform_fees.py tests/base/test_entitlements.py -q` — 25 passed
- `ruff check eventyay/base/platform_fees.py tests/base/test_platform_fees.py`
- `ruff format --check eventyay/base/platform_fees.py tests/base/test_platform_fees.py`
- `python manage.py check` — no issues

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a validated, plugin-neutral platform fee policy resolution contract in Core.

New Features:
- Add a neutral Core signal and resolver for optional platform fee policies.
- Return an explicit zero-fee policy when no provider responds.

Bug Fixes:
- Reject invalid fee-provider responses and ambiguous multiple-provider results instead of applying an undefined fee.

Enhancements:
- Validate platform fee percentages, maximum amounts, and numeric finiteness through an immutable policy type.

Tests:
- Add coverage for default policies, provider responses, validation failures, invalid responses, and multiple providers.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Payment platform fees can be determined by a policy that sets a percentage and maximum amount. If no policy is provided, the fee defaults to zero.
  * Fee policies are validated, and conflicting policies or invalid values are rejected to prevent inconsistent fee calculations.
